summary: This article explains why the Dead Sea is the lowest place on land, why its water is so salty that people float, why almost nothing lives in it, and why it is shrinking.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “The Dead Sea: Lowest Place on Land” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: heavy for its size because it is packed closely
living things that are too small to see without a microscope
natural materials found in rocks, soil, and water

challengeTerms.def: the height of a place above or below sea level
the amount of a substance mixed into a liquid or another material

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people should work hard to save the Dead Sea from shrinking? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why the Dead Sea is so salty and why it is getting smaller.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review dense, microbes, and minerals, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use elevation, concentration, and buoyant in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
